precise_question: Does the pre-exposure fraction of E. coli cells neither growing nor dividing predict later ampicillin survivor frequency beyond a simple population-level model?
biological_decision: Predict population survival after a defined ampicillin exposure from pre-exposure growth history.
measured_outcome: Population survivor frequency after ampicillin; input is non-growing-cell fraction measured immediately before exposure.
input_timing: Pre-exposure, before antibiotic; Umetani Fig. 7 defines non-growth/no division during the preceding 1.5 h.
independent_unit: Culture/condition would be the biological replicate; published plotted source data and run grouping were not inspected because the novelty gate failed.
direct_old_asset_transfer: Transfer only the idea that biological response may depend on a measured distribution, not the EV model equation or parameters.
closest_prior_art: Umetani et al. 2025 eLife Fig. 7B-C and Eq. 1 (f=sP_n); Kaplan et al. 2021 Nature links lag-time distributions to persistence survival.
exact_increment: No surviving increment for this exact predictor/outcome pair: the closest paper already tests their relationship and fits the simple model; a distinct input/outcome contrast would alter the fixed candidate.
dataset: Umetani Fig. 7/Supplementary source data and Dryad 10.5061/dryad.s1rn8pkb1; not downloaded.
access: Full paper and Dryad metadata inspected; source data archive listed but not fetched after novelty failure.
reason: Novelty gate fails before data-gate advancement; no pilot or extra data retrieval.

precise_question: Would subsampling baseline single-bnAb susceptibility change selection among a fixed set of bnAb pairs, and would that pair retain measured combination IC80 coverage on viruses withheld from selection?
biological_decision: Choose a bnAb pair under a fixed IC80 coverage rule using a finite baseline pseudovirus panel.
measured_outcome: Measured combination neutralization IC80 on held-out pseudoviruses; single-bnAb IC50/IC80 supplies the panel-selection input.
input_timing: Single-bnAb panel precedes the held-out decision in the proposed analysis; all source data are retrospective, not prospective clinical validation.
independent_unit: Virus/isolate is the assay unit; donor/lineage mapping and replicate grouping were not reconstructed, so independent biological group count is unresolved.
direct_old_asset_transfer: Transfer distribution-sensitive decision framing only; do not reuse the unrelated EV capture equation.
closest_prior_art: Wagh et al. 2016 PLoS Pathogens Fig. 2 measures 10 combinations on 20 selected viruses and compares observed/predicted combo IC80; Williamson et al. 2024 PLoS One uses observed single-antibody data but calculates combination outcomes; LaMont et al. 2022 eLife models clinical rebound and ranks cocktails.
exact_increment: Potentially distinct residual calculation is rank/choice stability under finite-panel subsampling evaluated against measured combo coverage. It is not established as a substantial biological increment beyond whole-panel combination ranking, held-out prediction and synthetic-sample-size work; no prospective decision consequence shown.
dataset: Wagh 200-virus single-agent panel and 20-virus selected combination subset; Williamson CATNAP single-agent rows; local HIV H5 is processed clinical/model output and not matched neutralization data.
access: Wagh measured combo points are public in Fig. 2/paper-SI; exact raw matched rows/group IDs not reconstructed. Williamson repo's CATNAP source concerns individual bnAbs; combo values in paper are calculated.
reason: Novelty/comparator increment unresolved and data gate partial: selected 20-virus measurements are not yet a verified independent, representative finite-panel evaluation; do not call all 200-virus combo scores empirical.
